steps.content:
December 26, N.F. 72
New DisCity

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Today, I stand before you as the second Commander of the DisCity Independence Army... and as your new Speaker of the City Council.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: This position wasn't given to me by the metropoles. It wasn't bought for us by corporate interests. It was earned by the will of every DisCitizen who cast a vote. It is your trust I carry.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: It means the metropoles' chains are broken. The predators are still at our gates, but we have taken back our dignity. We have taken back our freedom. And we will never give them up again.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: The days of being exploited, subdued, and oppressed are over. As of today, this city-state is ours. From this day forward, the fate of DisCity will be decided by DisCitizens alone.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: We stand here because countless heroes gave everything to get us to this starting line. We will honor their sacrifice, and we will carry their legacy forward.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Let the challenges come, from catastrophe or from man. We will meet them. We will build. We will protect. We will expand! Our city has risen. And it belongs to its people—its greatest strength.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: I hereby declare: DisCity is independent!

December 27, N.F. 74
DisCity Cemetery
Memorial Day of the Satellite Town Strategy Victory

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: "In order to preserve a core strategic military asset and prevent further damage from the escalating Mania contamination within the subject's body, DisCorps has decreed, with technical support from EDGE, that Sinner Catherine Augustus Andohar will be placed in cryostasis, effective—"

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: HA? ...The hell is this?
She lashed out with a kick aimed at Dravyn, DisCorps's Commander and first elected Speaker. But with the practiced ease of years, he sidestepped the blow.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: You're a vital asset that needs protecting. I have no intention of watching DisCity's youngest general turn into a monster, and being the one who has to put you down.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: The war is almost over. Your skills are no longer required. Say your goodbyes properly, then go to sleep. You'd hate peacetime anyway.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hmph. If you lot had done your jobs and developed a Mania treatment sooner, I wouldn't be the one headed for the freezer.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: The scientists at EDGE have done everything they can. 01 nearly worked himself to death developing this cryo-process to save you. A little gratitude wouldn't hurt. We'll wake you when it's time.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Or should I set an alarm? When would you like me to pencil you in?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: If I said "soon," that'd be like wishing for another war. Lieutenant would never let me live it down.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Then wake me when you've all retired, lived your lives, and are about to kick the bucket. I'll give you a proper send-off. Make sure your funerals are spectacular.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: You're the great heroes of DisCity. You can't just fade away quietly.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Heh. Who knows? Maybe I'm hoping for a day when the world changes completely. A day with no more war, no need for your kind of power at all.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: When that day comes, I'll wake you just to say it: "Soldiers like you are obsolete. Time to be a good girl and go get an education."

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hah! What a dream. You'd better deliver on that, Mr. Speaker of the City Council.

She almost scoffed. Why did the old geezer look so reluctant to let her go? It wasn't as if he'd be alone—he had Victor and Adrian. EDGE still had 01 to cure his baldness. She was the one who would be lying alone for ages. She was the one who should be worried about loneliness.

Time was almost up. She took one last look at DisCity. This was never the city-state that had earned her loyalty, yet for years it had been her battlefield. The place where she had found her most treasured blades. She turned around—

And faced the warriors who had fought beside her across countless battlefields. In every resolute face, she saw the same defiant pride. They were the sharpest blades, forged by their own will, living on their own terms.

Catherine slowly drew her sword and placed it in their steady hands. Then, she took a medal that belonged to the Eighth Division of DisCorps, the general's insignia that Dravyn awarded her with a manner almost that of an adult placating a child.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Take care of my troops. They're my pride.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: You have my word.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Well then, goodbye. I'll be waiting for the day I wake up.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: I'll be waiting for that day too.
